question: The compound interest earned in 1 year on ₹40,000 at the rate of 40% per annum, compounded quarterly, is:
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = ₹ 40,000

Time = 1 year

Rate = 40% per annum

**Concept Used:**

CI = P(1+(r\%/n)/(100))ⁿt-P

P = Principal amount

r = Rate of interest

t = time in years

n = Number of times the amount is compounding.

**Calculation:**

As it is compounded quarterly, so n = 4

Putting the values,

⇒ CI = 40000(1+(40over4)/(100))⁴ – 40000

⇒ CI = 40000times ((11)/(10))⁴ – 40000

⇒ CI = 40000times (121)/(100)times (121)/(100) – 40000

⇒ CI = 58564 – 40000 = ₹ 18,564

**Therefore, the compound interest for the sum when compounded quarterly is ₹ 18,564.**
